n2.d3.content: {"id":"vltg-orders-h1","title":"Voltaris Grid H1 2026 results: orders and backlog","body":"Voltaris Grid reported H1 2026 orders up 11% year on year, led by utility and data-centre customers. Backlog reached C$5.1B, which management says covers its 2027 revenue guidance of C$4.2B. Customer cancellations remained below 1%. Q2 output was affected by an incident at the Halbrook plant; see the separate release on its restart."}

n3.r1.content:
**Industry statistics point to 2027 revenue of about C$3.4–3.7B, well short of the C$4.2B guidance. The guidance would need roughly 12–18% growth against data showing a decline.**

- **Industry volume:** Caldrian transformer shipments fell 4% y/y in Q2 2026 (n3.d2). That is the first decline in three years, after +3.1% in Q4 2025 and +1.8% in Q1 2026 (n3.d5). Shipments typically trail orders by about two quarters, so the weakness probably carries into late 2026 and early 2027.
- **Voltaris share:** Share of shipments fell from 31% to 27% in Q2 2026 (n3.d3). That is a 13% relative loss, with Tarnwell and imports taking it. Voltaris shipments fell 9% (n3.d2), the steepest among large makers.
- **Revenue base:** Quarterly revenue was C$905M, C$960M, C$980M and C$890M from 2025Q3 to 2026Q2 (n3.d4). The last four quarters sum to C$3.735B. The Q2 2026 run-rate is C$3.56B annualised, down 9% from Q1.
- **Required growth:** C$4.2B is about 12% above the last four quarters and about 18% above the Q2 run-rate.

**Scenarios**, using the Q2 run-rate of C$3.56B as the base:

| Scenario | Assumption | 2027 revenue |
|---|---|---|
| Base | Industry flat to +2%, share stays near 27% | about C$3.5–3.65B |
| Bull | Industry recovers +5%, share regains to about 29% | about C$3.9B |
| Bear | Industry down a further 3–5%, share slips again | about C$3.2–3.4B |

I did not model price increases or backlog conversion. Voltaris's own orders and backlog may support higher revenue, and n2 is covering that.

The bull case still falls short of C$4.2B. Reaching it would need both an industry rebound and a recovery to the old 31% share.

n2.r1.content:
**Voltaris's own disclosures support 2027 revenue of roughly C$3.9–4.3B, with C$4.2B reachable but with little cushion.**

- **Backlog:** It is C$5.1B (H1 2026 results, n2.d3). Management says this covers the C$4.2B guidance, which is about 121% coverage. Hitting guidance means converting about 82% of the current backlog. That is plausible, but I found no disclosure on how fast the backlog converts or how much of it falls in 2027.
- **Orders:** H1 orders were up 11% year on year, led by utility and data-centre customers. Cancellations were below 1%, so the backlog looks firm.
- **Run-rate:** Quarterly revenue (series vltg_quarterly) was C$905M in 2025Q3, C$960M in 2025Q4, C$980M in 2026Q1 and C$890M in 2026Q2. The pre-fire pace of about C$970M a quarter annualizes to about C$3.9B. Reaching C$4.2B needs about C$1.05B a quarter, which is roughly 8% above that pace.
- **Halbrook plant:** Voltaris's largest plant was offline for nine weeks in Q2 after a fire (n2.d6). It restarted in August at full capacity. Management expects to recover the lost shipments by mid-2027, which would push catch-up revenue into H1 2027 and help the 2027 total.
- **Q2 shortfall:** The Q2 revenue was only about C$90M below the Q1 level. That limits how much catch-up there is to recover.

**Risks:**
- The fire shortfall is recovered only if the plant can run above normal output, and management gave no evidence of that.
- The guidance needs growth of about 8–10% over the 2026 run-rate, which is close to the 11% order growth. That leaves little room if conversion slips.

**Conflict with n3:** n3's industry-statistics view (n3.r1) puts 2027 revenue at about C$3.4–3.7B, well short of C$4.2B. My company-disclosure view is more favourable. The gap is mostly the backlog and Halbrook catch-up, which industry data may not capture. I did not look into why n3's industry figures come out lower.

n1.r1.content:
**Probably not. I put the chance of Voltaris Grid (VLTG) reaching C$4.2B in 2027 revenue at roughly 25–30%.** My expected range is about C$3.6–4.0B.

The two child analyses disagree. Which one is right comes down to whether the C$5.1B backlog converts to revenue on schedule.

- **Company disclosures (n2):**
  - The C$5.1B backlog is about 121% of guidance, so guidance needs about 82% of it to convert. n2 found no disclosure on how fast that happens.
  - H1 orders rose 11% and cancellations were under 1%.
  - Revenue before the Halbrook plant fire ran at about C$970M a quarter, or about C$3.9B a year. Guidance needs about C$1.05B a quarter, roughly 8% more.
  - Management expects to recover the fire-lost shipments by mid-2027.
  - n2's range is C$3.9–4.3B, with guidance reachable but little cushion.
- **Industry statistics (n3):**
  - Industry transformer shipments fell 4% in Q2 2026, the first decline in three years.
  - Voltaris's share of shipments fell from 31% to 27%, and its own shipments fell 9%.
  - The last four quarters of revenue sum to C$3.735B. Guidance is about 12% above that and about 18% above the Q2 run-rate.
  - n3's range is C$3.4–3.7B. Even its bull case, an industry rebound plus recovering to about 29% share, only reaches about C$3.9B.
  - n3 did not model price increases or backlog conversion.

The gap between the two ranges is mostly the backlog and the Halbrook catch-up. n2 did not explain why the industry data comes out lower, and n3 did not model the backlog.

I lean below guidance for three reasons:
- The backlog sits alongside falling shipments and lost share, and n2 found no evidence Halbrook can run above normal output to catch up.
- The pre-fire run-rate alone gives only about C$3.9B, and Q2 revenue has already fallen.
- Guidance needs both order growth to convert and share to stabilize.

Backlog conversion would settle it, and so would the 2026 Q3 and Q4 results. Revenue returning to about C$1B or more a quarter would make guidance realistic.
